root_cause.text: arm64 GCS mappings were built from the static _PAGE_GCS/_PAGE_GCS_RO PTE templates, which always included PTE_SHARED, but on FEAT_LPA2 systems those bits are repurposed as output-address bits so the resulting GCS PTEs became invalid and caused translation faults.
root_cause.evidence: The patch notes that “bits 8-9 of the PTE replace the shareability attribute with bits 50-51 of the output address” under LPA2, that the `_PAGE_GCS{,_RO}` definitions “include the PTE_SHARED bits as 0b11,” and fixes this by introducing `gcs_page_prot` and clearing `PTE_SHARED` when `lpa2_is_enabled()` before using it in `vm_get_page_prot()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant `PAGE_GCS` and `PAGE_GCS_RO` macro wrappers around the existing GCS page-protection flags.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the two macro definitions `PAGE_GCS` and `PAGE_GCS_RO`, which previously wrapped `_PAGE_GCS` and `_PAGE_GCS_RO` with `__pgprot(...)`. No other lines in the shown hunk are changed.
intent_record.how: By deleting these macros, the codebase no longer exposes those specific page-protection aliases at this location, so any remaining users must rely on the underlying `_PAGE_GCS` and `_PAGE_GCS_RO` values or other definitions. In the shown hunk itself, runtime behavior is unchanged unless other code depended on these macros being available.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a dedicated read-only GCS page protection descriptor for later use by the memory subsystem.
intent_record.what: A new static variable named `gcs_page_prot` of type `ptdesc_t` was added and initialized at compile time with `_PAGE_GCS_RO`, and it is marked `__ro_after_init`.
intent_record.how: This introduces a read-only-after-initialization page protection descriptor that can be reused by the memory management code for GCS-related pages, enabling the kernel to represent that protection state explicitly at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure `gcs_page_prot` also has `PTE_SHARED` cleared when LPA2 is enabled.
intent_record.what: The code now wraps the existing `lpa2_is_enabled()` check in braces and, inside that conditional block, adds a new statement that clears `PTE_SHARED` from `gcs_page_prot` in addition to the existing loop that clears `PTE_SHARED` from every entry in `protection_map`.
intent_record.how: When LPA2 is enabled, the shared bit is now removed not only from all protection map entries but also from the `gcs_page_prot` page protection value, preventing GCS pages from retaining the shared attribute under this configuration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the configured GCS page protection for shadow stack mappings instead of a hardcoded read-only value.
intent_record.what: In vm_get_page_prot(), the code handling the VM_SHADOW_STACK case changes the assigned protection value from the fixed constant _PAGE_GCS_RO to the variable gcs_page_prot.
intent_record.how: At runtime, shadow stack mappings on systems with GCS support will now use the page protection value stored in gcs_page_prot instead of always using the read-only GCS constant, allowing the protection configuration to follow the configured GCS page protection semantics.

Add a dedicated read-only GCS page protection descriptor for later use by the memory subsystem.

relevance_review.reason: The change is only removing redundant macro wrappers around existing GCS protection flags. It does not address the LPA2-specific invalid PTE construction caused by PTE_SHARED being repurposed as output-address bits, nor does it modify the underlying GCS PTE templates or mapping logic.

The change introduces a dedicated read-only GCS page protection descriptor, which is directly related to how GCS PTEs are constructed. This matches the root cause involving incorrect GCS PTE templates and invalid mappings on FEAT_LPA2 systems.
The change directly addresses the root cause: it clears PTE_SHARED from GCS page protections on LPA2 systems, fixing the invalid PTE encoding that caused translation faults.

The change targets GCS shadow stack page protection/mapping behavior, which is directly related to the root cause in arm64 GCS PTE construction. Using the configured GCS protection instead of a hardcoded template is the kind of fix needed to avoid invalid PTEs on FEAT_LPA2 systems.

candidates.rationale: This hardcoded GCS read-only PTE template is the direct source of the bug: it was built from static GCS flags that included PTE_SHARED, which becomes invalid on FEAT_LPA2 systems and leads to bad GCS mappings.
This loop only clears PTE_SHARED from the generic protection_map entries; before the fix, the separate GCS page protection entry was not covered, leaving its stale PTE_SHARED bit in place on LPA2.

vuln_statements.explanation: This hardcoded GCS read-only page protection uses the static _PAGE_GCS_RO template, which retained PTE_SHARED. On FEAT_LPA2 systems that bit is repurposed into output-address bits, making the resulting GCS PTE invalid and causing translation faults.

commit 6497b66ba6945f142902c7e8fce86e47016ead1c
Author: Mark Brown <broonie@kernel.org>
Date:   Tue Oct 1 23:58:54 2024 +0100

    arm64/mm: Map pages for guarded control stack
    
    Map pages flagged as being part of a GCS as such rather than using the
    full set of generic VM flags.
    
    This is done using a conditional rather than extending the size of
    protection_map since that would make for a very sparse array.
    
    Reviewed-by: Thiago Jung Bauermann <thiago.bauermann@linar
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is absent here. The function now has an explicit GCS-specific path: `if (system_supports_gcs() && (vm_flags & VM_SHADOW_STACK)) { prot = _PAGE_GCS_RO; }`, instead of always indexing the generic `protection_map`. The root cause was that GCS mappings were built from static `_PAGE_GCS/_PAGE_GCS_RO` templates that always included `PTE_SHARED`, which broke on LPA2. This snippet does not show any unconditional use of those old templates; it short-circuits GCS mapping via a dedicated conditional, which is the fix. The relevant lines are: `/* Short circuit GCS to avoid bloating the table. */` and `prot = _PAGE_GCS_RO;` guarded by `system_supports_gcs()` and `VM_SHADOW_STACK`.
